symbols.name: bilinear form
symbols.meaning: The scalar in F that the form assigns to the vectors x and y of E.
symbols.quote: A bilinear form on $E$ is a special case of a [bilinear map](bilinear-map.md) whose two arguments both come from $E$: it takes vectors $x$ and $y$ of $E$ to a scalar $\langle x,y\rangle$ in $F$, and it is linear in $x$ when $y$ is fixed and linear in $y$ when $x$ is fixed.

symbols.name: subspace
symbols.meaning: A subspace of E whose orthogonal complement is taken.

symbols.name: orthogonal complement
symbols.meaning: The set of vectors of E orthogonal to every vector of U.
symbols.quote: Its *orthogonal complement* $U^\perp$ is the set of vectors $x$ in $E$ with $\langle x,y\rangle=0$ for every $y$ in $U$.

symbols.name: basis vector
symbols.meaning: The j-th vector of the fixed basis of E.
symbols.quote: Fix a basis $e_1,\dots,e_m$ of $E$, so $m$ is the dimension of $E$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$-th basis vector.

symbols.name: transpose
symbols.meaning: The matrix obtained from M by swapping its rows and columns.
symbols.quote: For a matrix $M$, its transpose $M^{\top}$ has entries $(M^{\top})_{ij}=M_{ji}$.

symbols.name: coordinate
symbols.meaning: The i-th coordinate of the vector x in the basis e_1 through e_m.
symbols.quote: Let $x_i$ be the $i$-th coordinate of $x$, so $x=\sum_i x_ie_i$, and let $y_j$ be the $j$-th coordinate of $y$.

symbols.name: coordinate of y
symbols.meaning: The j-th coordinate of the vector y in the basis e_1 through e_m.
symbols.quote: Let $x_i$ be the $i$-th coordinate of $x$, so $x=\sum_i x_ie_i$, and let $y_j$ be the $j$-th coordinate of $y$.

symbols.name: form matrix
symbols.meaning: The m by m matrix whose entry in row i and column j is the form value of e_i and e_j.
symbols.quote: Let $\Psi$ be the $m\times m$ matrix with entries $\Psi_{ij}=\langle e_i,e_j\rangle$.

symbols.name: index set
symbols.meaning: The set of the first h positive integers.
symbols.quote: Write $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ for the set of the first $h$ positive integers.

symbols.name: triple
symbols.meaning: A three-element subset of [h], one of the triples whose indicator vectors are used.
symbols.quote: For a triple $T$, a three-element subset of $[h]$, let $t_T$ be its indicator vector, with entry 1 at each element of $T$ and 0 elsewhere.

symbols.name: indicator vector
symbols.meaning: The 0-1 vector with entry 1 at each element of the triple T and 0 elsewhere.
symbols.quote: For a triple $T$, a three-element subset of $[h]$, let $t_T$ be its indicator vector, with entry 1 at each element of $T$ and 0 elsewhere.

symbols.name: second triple
symbols.meaning: A second three-element subset of [h], whose indicator vector is t_S.
symbols.quote: For triples $S$ and $T$ (each a three-element subset of $[h]$, with indicator vector $t_S$ or $t_T$), $\mathbf 1^{\top}t_S=\mathbf 1^{\top}t_T=3$ and $t_S^{\top}t_T=|S\cap T|$, which counts the common elements.

relations.quote: A bilinear form on $E$ is a special case of a [bilinear map](bilinear-map.md) whose two arguments both come from $E$: it takes vectors $x$ and $y$ of $E$ to a scalar $\langle x,y\rangle$ in $F$, and it is linear in $x$ when $y$ is fixed and linear in $y$ when $x$ is fixed.
In coordinates, the form is written with the matrices of [linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md).
Nondegeneracy is decided by the [eigenvalues](eigenvalue.md) of $\Psi$, since $\Psi$ is invertible exactly when none of them is zero.
